tradition.name: Telugu
tradition.description: Varjyam, Durmuhurtham, Rahu Kalam, Yamagandam, Gulika and Amrita Kalam.

RahuKalam.name: Rahu Kalam
RahuKalam.meaning: A daily period associated with Rahu that is traditionally considered unfavorable for beginning important or auspicious activities. Its timing is calculated using the local sunrise, sunset, and weekday.
RahuKalam.description: A traditionally unfavorable period for important new beginnings.

Yamagandam.name: Yamagandam
Yamagandam.meaning: A daily period associated with Yama that is traditionally considered unfavorable for beginning auspicious activities. It is calculated from the local sunrise, sunset, and weekday.
Yamagandam.description: A period traditionally avoided when starting important or auspicious activities.

DurMuhurtam.name: Durmuhurtham
DurMuhurtam.meaning: A period of the day considered unfavorable when selecting an auspicious Muhurta. Depending on the weekday, there may be more than one Dur Muhurtam period.
DurMuhurtam.description: An unfavorable Muhurta traditionally avoided for important beginnings.

GulikaKalam.name: Gulika Kalam
GulikaKalam.meaning: A daily period associated with Gulika and traditionally linked with Saturn. It is generally treated with caution when choosing an auspicious starting time.
GulikaKalam.description: A period traditionally treated with caution for auspicious new beginnings.

Varjyam.name: Varjyam
Varjyam.meaning: A Nakshatra-based period traditionally considered unsuitable for auspicious beginnings. Unlike Rahu Kalam, its timing is derived from the day's Nakshatra and may occur during the day or night.
Varjyam.description: A Nakshatra-based period traditionally considered unfavorable for auspicious beginnings.

AmritKalam.name: Amrita Kalam
AmritKalam.meaning: A highly auspicious period derived from Nakshatra-based calculations and traditionally associated with favorable energy and positive beginnings.
AmritKalam.description: A highly auspicious period considered favorable for important and positive activities.

tithi.name: Tithi
tithi.meaning: The lunar day. Each Tithi corresponds to 12° of separation between the Moon and the Sun, giving 30 Tithis in a lunar month: 15 in the waxing (Shukla) fortnight and 15 in the waning (Krishna) fortnight. A Tithi can begin at any time of day and lasts roughly 19 to 26 hours.
tithi.description: The lunar day, based on the angle between the Moon and the Sun.

nakshatra.name: Nakshatra
nakshatra.meaning: One of the 27 lunar mansions, each spanning 13°20′ of the sidereal zodiac. The day's Nakshatra is the one the Moon is passing through; it changes about once a day.
nakshatra.description: The lunar mansion the Moon is passing through.

yoga.name: Yoga
yoga.meaning: One of 27 combinations obtained by adding the sidereal longitudes of the Sun and the Moon and dividing by 13°20′. Each Yoga is traditionally associated with a favorable or unfavorable quality.
yoga.description: A daily combination of the Sun's and the Moon's positions.

karana.name: Karana
karana.meaning: Half of a Tithi, corresponding to 6° of Moon–Sun separation. There are 11 Karanas: 7 that repeat through the lunar month and 4 fixed ones. Vishti (Bhadra) is traditionally avoided for auspicious activities.

sunrise.name: Sunrise
sunrise.meaning: The moment the upper edge of the Sun appears on the horizon at the location, allowing for atmospheric refraction. The Panchang day begins at sunrise, and Rahu Kalam, the Muhurtas and other periods are measured from it.
sunrise.description: The start of the Panchang day at this location.

sunset.name: Sunset
sunset.meaning: The moment the upper edge of the Sun disappears below the horizon at the location. Daytime periods such as Rahu Kalam divide the time between sunrise and sunset.
sunset.description: The end of daytime at this location.

vara.name: Vara
vara.meaning: The weekday. In the Panchang a weekday runs from one sunrise to the next, and several daily periods, including Rahu Kalam, Yamagandam and Gulika Kalam, depend on it.
vara.description: The day of the week, counted from sunrise.

HighlyFavorable.name: Highly Favorable
HighlyFavorable.description: Today's Panchang factors are strongly supportive for common activities.

Favorable.name: Favorable
Favorable.description: Today's Panchang factors are generally supportive for common activities.

Mixed.name: Mixed
Mixed.description: Today's Panchang factors are mixed; choose timings carefully for important activities.

Caution.name: Caution
Caution.description: Several of today's Panchang factors call for caution; prefer the recommended time periods for important activities.

Avoid.name: Traditionally Avoided
Avoid.description: Today's Panchang factors are traditionally considered unfavorable for new beginnings.

Avoid for new beginnings: Rahu Kalam 08:23–10:07 CDT, Yamagandam 11:52–13:36 CDT, Durmuhurtham 14:04–15:00 CDT, Durmuhurtham 16:51–17:47 CDT, Varjyam 03:00(+1)–04:25(+1) CDT. Use caution: Gulika Kalam 15:21–17:05 CDT. Check the recommended and traditionally avoided time periods below before beginning an important activity.

factors.name: Amavasya
factors.reason: Tithi Amavasya: Traditionally Avoided. New moon, traditionally avoided for auspicious beginnings and observed for ancestral rites.

factors.name: Monday
factors.reason: Vara Monday: Favorable. A gentle (Saumya) weekday, traditionally supportive of auspicious work.

factors.name: Ardra
factors.reason: Nakshatra Ardra: Traditionally Avoided. A sharp (Tikshna) Nakshatra, traditionally avoided for auspicious beginnings.

factors.name: Vyaghata
factors.reason: Yoga Vyaghata: Caution. One of the malefic Yogas, traditionally treated with caution.

factors.name: Chatushpada
factors.reason: Karana Chatushpada: Caution. A fixed Karana (Shakuni, Chatushpada, Naga), traditionally treated with caution.

guidance.methodology: Daily guidance summarizes the five Panchanga limbs (Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra, Yoga, Karana) using this app's methodology. It is not a universal traditional rule and not a Muhurta for a specific ceremony such as a marriage or housewarming.
